I have been working this land since I was a child helping my parents, so I know this soil and this weather. My farm is small — 4.1 mu — and my husband works in the city some months, so I handle most of the farm myself. I cannot read the bags carefully but I know what the village store sells and what my neighbors use. I follow what has worked for me year after year.

**My wheat:** I plant in October after the corn comes off. I use the improved seeds from the township supply station — they give better yields than the old seeds my mother used. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and add urea in spring when the wheat turns green. I irrigate from the well — at overwintering, green-up, jointing, and heading — four times. I spray once for weeds in winter and once for aphids and mildew in spring. I use rotary tillage to turn the stubble in before planting.

**My maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize. I use hybrid seed — everyone does now, the yield is much better. I put fertilizer down at planting and topdress when the plant is knee-high. I irrigate at planting if it's dry, at tasseling, and at grain fill — three times usually. I spray herbicide right after planting and check once more for stem borer. For tillage I just do a light rotary pass.

My son sometimes helps on weekends. With only 4.1 mu I can manage this myself mostly.
